jobs.title: Director, Analytics Engineering
jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An Overview Of This Role

As Director, Analytics Engineering, you'll lead a team of 8 and report to the VP of Data & Insights. You set direction across the data organization, stay close enough to the work to guide technical decisions credibly, and partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, IT, and business leaders.

You Will Have Three Mandates

Build trusted, AI-ready self-service. Deliver a semantic model that answers business questions correctly, with the telemetry, evals, and model flexibility to prove it and keep costs in check.
Set the strategy for how GitLab accesses data. Own the data models, BI tools, and AI access patterns (Claude, MCP servers, Slack agents) that put trusted data in everyone's hands.
Build data applications the whole company relies on. Ship production-grade apps that combine trusted data, APIs, and AI to answer questions dashboards can't.

What You'll Do

Build and own a trusted semantic model, with governed metrics and business definitions, that answers business questions consistently across every tool
Build evals and ground-truth datasets that measure answer quality, and use them to drive improvements and catch regressions
Instrument telemetry to see who uses the semantic model and AI tools, what they ask, and where they get stuck
Build a model-selection harness so GitLab can route work across LLMs and stay flexible on cost and quality
Own data modeling and curated datasets for self-service, with the ownership, data contracts, testing, and documentation that make them AI-ready
Define the AI data access strategy: when to use BI, Claude, MCP servers, or Slack agents, with the governance and security to keep access trusted and reliable
Own the enterprise BI and self-service tools strategy (e.g., Tableau, Omni), including evaluation, adoption, and cost
Build self-service capabilities, such as Claude skills, documentation, and guided workflows, that help people find and use data on their own
Build and own company-wide data applications, from Claude-built single-page apps to apps inside BI tools, that combine Snowflake data, API calls, AI-powered deep dives, and write-back to Postgres or Snowflake
Set engineering standards for data apps (security, authentication, testing, deployment, and monitoring) so they're reliable at company scale
Set a long-range roadmap tied to company strategy, and a lightweight operating model that balances urgent stakeholder needs with investment in reusable data products and tech-debt reduction
Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of 8: build career paths, develop leaders, distribute ownership, and recognize great work
Act as customer zero for GitLab and GitLab Duo in data workflows, sharing feedback with Product and Engineering

What You'll Bring

12+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI, including 5+ years leading teams and 2+ years managing managers or senior leads
Deep expertise in data modeling and semantic layers (e.g., dbt Semantic Layer, Snowflake semantic views, LookML, Cube), and expert dbt, including testing and CI/CD across a multi-team project
Hands-on experience building LLM-powered data access (text-to-SQL, agents, MCP servers), including evals and telemetry for answer quality, and advanced use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code
Expert SQL and strong Snowflake experience; working knowledge of Python
Strong data governance experience: data quality, lineage, certified datasets, and access controls (RBAC, row access and masking policies)
Track record of leading cross-functional data initiatives from strategy through adoption and measurable business impact, including enterprise BI and self-service at scale
Systems thinker who sees how models, pipelines, and architecture decisions connect, and designs for second-order effects
Exceptional communicator who writes clear technical specs, sets a clear vision, makes trade-offs visible, and influences executives and peers across the company
Pragmatic in ambiguity: makes sound decisions on emerging technology and ships the right next version rather than waiting for the ideal end state
Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values

Nice to Have

Experience with LLM routing or gateway tools and managing model costs
Experience with Tableau, Omni, or a BI platform migration
Experience with web app development (e.g., React, TypeScript) and Postgres
Experience owning finance or revenue-critical data (e.g., ARR, consumption) where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable

About The Team

Analytics Engineering makes GitLab's data trusted, easy to find, and ready for anyone to use, whether they ask a dashboard, Claude, or a Slack agent. We own the curated data models, the semantic layer, the self-service tools, and the data applications that let teams answer their own questions.

AI is changing how people get to data. Questions that once went through an analyst now go straight to AI tools, so the answers are only as good as the data models and business definitions behind them. Our job is to make those answers correct, consistent, and measurable.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
Flexible Paid Time Off

jobs.description:
Director of Finance / Director of Accounting | Vancouver & Lower Mainland
Location:
Vancouver, BC and surrounding Lower Mainland
Employment:
Permanent and Contract Opportunities
Compensation:
Typically $150,000 to $210,000+ annually, depending on experience and opportunity

The Opportunity
Torus Talent is connecting with senior finance and accounting leaders across British Columbia as we continue to develop our executive and senior management talent network.
We are interested in speaking with experienced Directors of Finance, Directors of Accounting, Senior Controllers, and other accomplished finance professionals who are considering their next leadership opportunity.

Our clients operate across a range of industries, including manufacturing, distribution, mining, technology, professional services, and other commercial sectors.
We are particularly interested in individuals who combine strong technical accounting expertise with commercial awareness, strategic thinking, and a proven ability to lead and develop finance teams.

Typical Responsibilities
Depending on the organization and mandate, responsibilities may include:
Providing leadership and strategic direction across finance and accounting functions.
Overseeing financial reporting, accounting operations, and regulatory compliance.
Leading annual budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and performance analysis.
Partnering with the CFO, CEO, and executive leadership on financial and operational strategy.
Developing financial policies, internal controls, and governance frameworks.
Managing cash flow, working capital, and financial risk.
Leading and mentoring Controllers, Accounting Managers, FP&A professionals, and accounting teams.
Supporting mergers, acquisitions, integrations, and business transformation initiatives.
Overseeing ERP implementations, financial systems, and process improvements.
Presenting financial results, business insights, and recommendations to executive leadership and stakeholders.
Supporting long-term financial planning and organizational growth.

Qualifications and Experience
We are interested in senior professionals who offer:
A CPA designation, with additional finance qualifications considered an asset.
10+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience.
Previous leadership experience as a Director of Finance, Director of Accounting, Corporate Controller, or similar.
Demonstrated success leading and developing accounting and finance teams.
Strong technical knowledge of ASPE, IFRS, and/or US GAAP.
Experience with financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and executive reporting.
A proven ability to partner with senior leadership on strategic and operational decisions.
Experience managing complex financial structures, multiple business units, or international operations.
Strong commercial judgment, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Experience in private equity-backed, high-growth, multi-entity, or publicly traded organizations would be particularly relevant.

Why Connect With Torus Talent?
At this level, finding the right opportunity involves alignment between leadership style, business strategy, organizational culture, and long-term career objectives.
Our team works with organizations seeking experienced finance leaders who can strengthen financial operations, support business growth, and contribute at the executive level.
We welcome confidential conversations with established finance leaders who are actively considering a move or would like to remain informed about future opportunities.

Interested in discussing your next leadership opportunity?

Submit your resume to join our senior finance and accounting talent network. Our team will contact you to better understand your experience, career interests, and the types of opportunities that may be relevant.

jobs.title: Director, Digital Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Our mission is to Drive Business Performance. We use data to create personalized and connected experiences that deliver transformative business outcomes. Our role is to ensure our clients meet their quantifiable business goals every day, consistently, in every market. We are entirely focused on delivering better business results through optimization, creation and analysis across all digital platforms. Our scope ranges from recommending how to use content more effectively to optimizing daily media channel performance and maximizing visibility in eCommerce platforms.

The Director, Digital Strategy is the senior strategic digital lead for the client account. The role defines how digital channels work together across the customer journey to support the client’s brand and business goals, and ensures digital thinking is embedded from the brief onward rather than added once activation begins.This is a client-facing leadership role focused on vision, integration and decision-making. The Director turns audience, cultural, platform, business and measurement signals into a focused digital strategy, clear priorities and practical roadmaps. The role brings choiceful recommendations, constructive challenge and a future-facing point of view.

The Director will work alongside Client Leadership and Planning, while partnering closely with the Digital Manager, channel specialists and Media Effectiveness. The Digital Manager and specialists remain responsible for in-platform strategy, buying, account structure, bidding, pacing, optimization, trafficking and quality assurance. The Director sets the strategic direction and ensures the work adds up to one connected digital proposition.

What Success Looks Like

The client can clearly articulate the digital channel strategy, the role of each channel and how the ecosystem supports business growth.
Digital strategy develops at the same pace as the broader media strategy and shapes investment, audience and measurement decisions from the outset.
The client receives concise, decisive recommendations that clarify what matters now, what comes next and why.
Testing, measurement and learning lead to visible changes in strategy, investment and activation.
First-party data, audience and innovation opportunities progress through practical, phased roadmaps with clear ownership and dependencies.
The account operates as one integrated client leadership, planning, digital activation and measurement team.

Key Accountabilities

Digital channel strategy and integration

Own the account’s digital channel strategy and roadmap, connecting business objectives, audience needs, customer journey, channel roles, investment priorities and measurement
Partner with Client Leadership and Planning from the brief onward so digital strategy is developed as part of the core media response, not as a downstream activation layer.
Define how paid Search, Social, Programmatic, Display, Video and other relevant digital channels work together across the funnel, while channel specialists determine the detailed in-platform approach.
Translate complex inputs into a focused set of priorities, choices and actions the client and team can understand and deliver.

Audience, innovation and growth agenda

Develop audience and segmentation strategies that connect broad media audiences, platform signals, app and loyalty opportunities, and first-party data ambitions.
Identify opportunities to improve brand impact, acquisition, engagement, loyalty and media effectiveness, and convert them into sequenced recommendations with clear expected value.
Bring a forward-looking point of view on changing consumer behaviour, platform evolution, AI-enabled media and emerging digital opportunities, distinguishing useful innovation from novelty.
Create a visible innovation agenda for the client that links new opportunities to real business questions, readiness and measurable outcomes.

Measurement, testing and learnin g

With Media Effectiveness and channel leads, define the learning agenda and ensure each priority has a clear business question, hypothesis, success measure and decision rule.
Connect reach, attention, engagement, conversion, efficiency and incrementality evidence to the business question being answered.
Turn reporting and specialist input into concise recommendations on what to continue, change, stop, scale or test next.
Ensure learning is applied back into audience, channel, investment and creative decisions, creating a continuous strategy-to-learning cycle.

First-party data and connected capabilities

Lead the media strategy and use-case components of the first-party data and audience maturity roadmap, in partnership with Media Effectiveness, CRM, loyalty, app, privacy, data and technology stakeholders.
Break complex ambitions into practical phases with explicit ownership, dependencies, decision points and realistic timelines.
First party data connecting to business strategy

Client leadership and team developmen t

Present the digital strategy and roadmap in senior meetings, annual planning, business reviews and critical transformation workstreams.
Coach the Digital Manager, planners and specialists to connect platform recommendations to the wider strategy and communicate with greater clarity and confidence.
Establish clear ways of working and decision rights across Client Leadership, Planning, Digital Activation, Media Effectiveness and specialist partners.

Qualifications

8+ years of progressive experience in digital media strategy, communications planning, digital transformation or integrated media, ideally across agency and/or client environments.
Post-secondary degree or diploma in Media, Advertising, Marketing, Business, Strategy, Analytics or a related field
Demonstrated experience building full-funnel digital channel strategies that connect business goals, audiences, channel roles, investment and measurement.
Strong understanding of the strategic roles and interdependencies of paid Search, Social, Programmatic, Display and Video. Current platform fluency is required; deep hands-on buying or platform-operations expertise is not the core requirement.
Experience translating audience, platform, analytics, research and business signals into a clear strategic point of view and actionable roadmap.
Practical understanding of first-party data, CRM, app and loyalty use cases, including the organizational and measurement dependencies required to activate them.
Experience shaping learning agendas and working with measurement specialists to turn evidence into decisions.
Exceptional client leadership, storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to simplify complexity and make decisive recommendations.
Experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing outcomes without relying solely on formal authority.

Additional Information

jobs.title: Director of finance
jobs.description:
REPORT TO: Head of School

POSITION GROUP: Senior Leadership Team

STATUS: Full-Time, Permanent

At Calgary French & International School (CFIS), exceptional education is supported by strong leadership, responsible stewardship, and a commitment to excellence. As we experience significant enrolment growth and campus expansion, we are seeking a strategic, forward-thinking Director of Finance
to help guide our financial sustainability and future development.

Guided by our values of We Care, We Connect, We Strive, and We Grow
, CFIS is a collaborative and ambitious school community. The Director of Finance will be a key member of our leadership team, bringing financial expertise, sound judgment, and strategic insight to support informed decision-making and responsible growth.

Anticipated Start Date:
December 1, 2026, or a mutually agreeable date for the successful candidate.

Purpose of the Position

CFIS’s Director of Finance will be a self-motivated, methodical and conscientious leader. The successful candidate will be a key contributor to the strategic plan and strategic financial plan, will ensure the financial health of the school and the feasibility of strategic decisions, and will support financial activities to allow the school’s Board of Directors to meet its fiscal responsibilities. They will oversee the operations of the school’s Finance and Human Resources Departments, and as such will lead, coach and manage two direct reports for high performance. 
The Director of Finance will be a member of the Senior Leadership Team and will work closely with the Head of School, Assistants Head of School and Departmental Directors.

Job Responsibilities: 

The position’s key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:
Prepare quarterly financial statements and variance analyses for the CFIS Society.
Implement and maintain effective financial policies and procedures to ensure financial integrity.
Provide senior leadership team with monthly departmental/divisional financial reports.
Work closely with senior leadership team and provide financial leadership and strategic insight to the Head of School.  
Lead and coach the Finance and Human Resources Departments to ensure that the department’s stakeholders see the departments as an operational partner in achieving their goals.
Business planning, budget development, and performance measurement.
Preparation of financial information for Alberta Education’s Annual Education Results Report and Three-Year Business Plan, and Annual Operating Plan.
Preparation of annual T3010 Registered Charity Information Return.
In collaboration with the Head of School and senior leadership team, prepare annual budget and financial strategic plan for the CFIS Society.
Maintain internal control system to support the growth and expansion of CFIS.
Lead the Business Office through the year-end external financial audit and any other financial audits by government bodies.
Lead, oversee, and evaluate the business units of the school’s operations and ensure appropriate process mapping, planning, organization, leadership, performance management, and accountability.
Annual issuance of childcare tax receipts.
Monthly issuance of charitable tax receipts and gift-in-kind tax receipts.
Verify and ensure bank covenant calculations on a quarterly basis.
Ensure compliance with Alberta Education’s Level 2 funding requirements and reporting.
Review the Finance and HR Department’s processes, technology and departmental structure to harness the benefits of automation, process modernization and finance effectiveness best practices. 
Continue to ensure the full integration of all business transactions and the accounting system. 
Prepare input for and analyze results of the CAIS benchmarking report.
Attend monthly meetings of the CFIS Society’s Board of Directors and Finance & Audit Committee. 

Qualifications : 

The ideal candidate will bring the following education, experience, skills and competencies:
A university degree from a recognized post-secondary institution and a Chartered Professional Accountant designation (or equivalent).
A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible experience in accounting, audit procedures, and financial operations.
A minimum of three years of experience leading a finance function or a team of at least five.
Demonstrated impact in non-profit or business organizations in a senior leadership position.
Extensive knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), consolidation theory and practice, modern controllership, financial and accounting theories and practices, in order to ensure the appropriate financial framework of the school, provide specialized financial expertise, advice and leadership, and to set accounting standards and ensure compliance.
Ability to present complex financial information to various audiences, and present convincing recommendations for effective and appropriate financial management. 
Solid analytical, organization, planning and problem-solving capabilities.
Able to think both strategically and tactically.
Excellent attention to detail.
Excellent communication skills, preferably in both English and French (English essential).

The successful candidate will need to provide, or have on file, an updated Police Information Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening prior to commencing work. 

Skills, Technical and Behavioural Competencies Required: 

Preference will be given to candidates who:
Are strong planners and organizers.
Have previous experience with non-profit financial management and operations.
Model best practices of exemplary professionalism in dealing with all stakeholders.
Possess strong interpersonal skills that foster collegiality and further the common goals of CFIS’s mission, vision and values.
Have previous experience working in an independent school.
Have experience with finance automation and process modernization. Sage 300 is the school’s current accounting platform.
Experience in the role of Chief Financial Officer in a not-for-profit organization would be beneficial.

Compensation:

We offer a competitive, comprehensive salary and benefits package as well as opportunities for professional growth.
Our benefits include:
Personal days
Sick days
Retirement Savings Benefit
60% tuition discount for children of full-time employees
Extended health and dental coverage
Health and Wellness Spending Accounts
Three weeks paid vacation time off in addition to two-weeks off at winter break and one-week off at March break when the school is closed.

Pay range:
$160,000 to $180,000 annual salary based on education and experience.

Application Process:

This job posting will remain open until filled.
If this position sounds like the perfect fit for you, please submit your cover letter and resume to Apply Now
. Don’t meet every single requirement? At CFIS we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role, but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway with a cover letter and resume describing why you are a great fit and to help us learn more about you. You may be just the right candidate! 

We thank all applicants in advance for their submission.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Finance Shared Services
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Senior Director, Finance Shared Services will have Canadian national responsibility for driving and managing all aspects of the Accounts Payable, Payroll, Accounts Receivable and Trade spend finance functions, including managing all relevant internal and external stakeholder relations as well as serving as a strategic partner to the Chief Financial Officer. The Senior Director Finance shared services provides counsel and strategic direction on related processes, governance and controls, and is responsible for service-level delivery including timeliness and accuracy.

They will play a key role in establishing the financial strategy to drive operational efficiency and enterprise value; through standardization of processes, service delivery, controls and compliance and other continuous improvement opportunities. They will work in partnership with the Chief Financial Officer and the business stakeholders to drive continued growth and attain the company’s strategic goals, as well as providing proactive support to leadership throughout the business. The successful candidate must be able to succinctly articulate the value proposition for the business, while driving process optimization and cost efficiency for the internal finance function, as well as for the business.

Key Responsibilities

Accounting and Financial Reporting

Establish, evaluate, and improve policies and procedures for effectiveness; implement changes to improve department performance and alignment with Company’s growth.
Oversee preparation of relevant daily, weekly monthly, quarterly and year-end financial reports.
Review month-end closing activities related to AP, payroll and AR and Trade Spend including subledger maintenance and balance sheet reconciliations.
Serve as a key point of contact for AP, payroll, AR and trade spend inquiries from external auditors as needed.
Manage shared services budget and operating costs.
Ensure data integrity, reporting accuracy, and system effectiveness.

Service Delivery Excellence

Lead the delivery of all shared services activities in cost efficient manner, while meeting agreed service levels.
Ensure Services are delivered accurately, efficiently, and consistent across the organization
Establish and monitor service levels and KPIs and customer satisfaction metrics.

Process Standardization and Continuous Improvement

Design, implement and continuously improve standardized end to end processes including process automation and process simplification initiatives.
Identify and eliminate inefficiencies, duplication, waste and non-value added activities
Benchmark performance against industry best practices.

Business Partnership and Customer Experience

Act as strategic partner to business leaders and functional executives
Develop strong relationships with internal stakeholders to understand needs and priorities

Governance, Controls and Compliance

Develop and maintain internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points.
Ensure adherence to regulatory, legal, audit, and corporate policy requirements.

Strategy and Executive Management

Develop and execute the shared services strategy and roadmap
Champion and lead organizational and process change initiatives.

Requirements

Shared Services professional with at least 10 years of increasingly responsible management experience.
The ideal candidate will have led the Finance Shared Services function for a business with similar size and complexity.
Strategic, “business-driven” finance instincts and business acumen.
Equally capable on both strategic and operational levels.
Must have a strong track record of having built, implemented and continuously improved shared services processes and systems to drive synergies, savings, and/or improved controls
Experience with integrating and implementing automation tools or information technology systems.
Early career foundation in accounting and control.
MBA and/or CPA an asset.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Commercial Banking (Corporate Finance Group)
jobs.description:
Corporate Finance Team Overview:

The Corporate Finance team within Canadian Commercial Banking, is part of BMO Financial group and covers both public and large private corporate clients operating in diversified industries. The team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Job Overview

The Associate Director plays a critical role in supporting the growth and risk‑management objectives of the portfolio. This role requires a combination of advanced financial analysis, strong credit analysis and relationship management abilities. Associate Directors contribute to client decisioning, credit structuring, and portfolio oversight, while also supporting new business development and delivering a superior client experience. Work is performed in close partnership with Managing Director and/or Director. The deal team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.

Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.
Assesses client repayment capacity by utilizing financial models and analytical tools to recommend appropriate loan structures and collateral requirements.
Signs off on new, renewal and extension loans within delegated authority.
Monitors portfolio to identify deteriorating credit conditions and compliance, analyses metrics, and assesses broader industry trends to spot risks and opportunities.
Evaluates portfolio performance and recommends capital allocation strategies that optimize returns with investment objectives.
Leads proposal development and delivers presentations to capture new business and expand client relationships.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Develops and executes business development plans focused on enhancing client relationships and growth opportunities within the portfolio.
Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.
Structures and supports new, renewal and extension loans aligned with client needs and bank & risk policies
Conducts financial analysis and risk assessments of clients’ credit information, for an assigned portfolio, to provide insights and make informed decisions
Monitors the portfolio performance for assigned portfolio of Commercial Banking clients on an ongoing basis, taking corrective action when required.
Minimizes BMO’s risk exposure by adhering to credit policies, regulatory standards, and operational guidelines.
Serves as a point of contact for service requests, ensuring expectations are consistently met or exceeded. Escalates issues when needed.
Supports and implements initiatives to enhance service quality, acquire new business and expand client relationships.
Identifies revenue and cross-selling opportunities to enhance portfolio growth.
Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
Manages timely and accurate data entry into BMO's systems and leverages the data to support decision-making.
Focus is primarily on business/group within BMO; may have broader, enterprise-wide focus.
Provides specialized consulting, analytical and technical support.
Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

Preferred 5 – 7 years of relevant experience in credit or lending instruments or financial operations in a corporate or banking environment.
If a Credit Qualifiable job, Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the credit portfolio requirements and qualification standards.
Bachelor’s degree required; Business Administration, Finance and Accounting preferred. Any other related discipline or commensurate work experience considered.
Deep knowledge and technical proficiency gained through extensive education and business experience.

Foundational level of proficiency:

Structuring Deals

Advanced level of proficiency:

Problem Solving
Collaboration
Detail-Oriented
Customer Service
Loan Structuring
Regulatory Compliance
Portfolio Management
Credit Risk Assessment
Banking Operations
Microsoft Office

Expert level of proficiency:

Financial analysis

Salary:

$70,000.00 - $150,000.00

Pay Type:

jobs.description:
At Equitable, we believe work should be a place where you feel supported, inspired, and empowered to grow. In our caring and collaborative environment, your curiosity is encouraged, your passion is recognized, and your contributions truly matter. Together, we create meaningful impact, for our clients, our communities, and each other.

The Opportunity:
  At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

As Director, Enterprise Third-Party Management, you will lead the development and oversight of Equitable’s enterprise-wide third-party management framework, ensuring third-party relationships deliver value, support strategic objectives, and operate within the Company's risk appetite and regulatory requirements. In this highly visible leadership role, you will oversee third-party governance, procurement, vendor management, and cost optimization initiatives while ensuring compliance with OSFI Guideline B-10 and other applicable regulations. Working closely with senior leaders across the organization, you will provide expert guidance on third-party strategy, risk management, commercial relationships, and operational resilience. You will also lead a high-performing team and help strengthen Equitable’s ability to manage third-party risk while driving business performance and operational efficiency.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements:
This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.

What you’ll do:

Develop, implement, and continuously enhance Equitable’s Third-Party Risk Management program, ensuring compliance with OSFI Guideline B-10 and other applicable regulatory requirements
Establish and maintain enterprise-wide standards for third-party due diligence, onboarding, risk assessment, oversight, performance monitoring, and termination processes
Provide oversight and effective challenge for significant third-party relationships across the organization, including MGAs, reinsurers, and vendors
Monitor emerging third-party risks, industry trends, and regulatory developments, recommending program enhancements to strengthen governance and risk management practices
Deliver regular reporting and insights to senior management and governance committees on third-party risks, program effectiveness, and key performance indicators
Lead procurement and vendor management activities, including strategic sourcing, supplier selection, contract negotiation, vendor governance, and supplier performance management
Drive enterprise vendor cost management initiatives focused on spend visibility, contract optimization, value realization, service quality, and operational efficiency
Lead and develop a high-performing team while partnering with Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Information Security, Privacy, and business leaders to support strategic initiatives, outsourcing arrangements, and business transformation programs

What you’ll bring:

University degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, Supply Chain Management, Commerce, Law, or a related field
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in third-party risk management, procurement, vendor management, operational risk, or a related discipline
Experience working within financial services, insurance, or another highly regulated industry
Strong knowledge of third-party risk management principles, governance frameworks, and regulatory expectations, including OSFI Guideline B-10
Demonstrated success leading procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier governance, contract management, and vendor performance programs
Proven ability to negotiate complex commercial agreements and deliver measurable cost optimization and value realization initiatives
Exceptional leadership, stakeholder management, communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across multiple business functions
Professional designation such as CPA, CFA, PMP, SCMP, or an equivalent credential is considered an asset, along with experience identifying, monitoring, and managing operational risks through effective controls, assessments, and testing

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities 
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching 
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year
Flexibility: Healthy work-life balance with employee wellness always top of mind, complemented by a “dress for your day” approach

new_jobs.description:
REPORT TO: Head of School

POSITION GROUP: Senior Leadership Team

STATUS: Full-Time, Permanent

At Calgary French & International School (CFIS), exceptional education is supported by strong leadership, responsible stewardship, and a commitment to excellence. As we experience significant enrolment growth and campus expansion, we are seeking a strategic, forward-thinking Director of Finance
to help guide our financial sustainability and future development.

Guided by our values of We Care, We Connect, We Strive, and We Grow
, CFIS is a collaborative and ambitious school community. The Director of Finance will be a key member of our leadership team, bringing financial expertise, sound judgment, and strategic insight to support informed decision-making and responsible growth.

Anticipated Start Date:
December 1, 2026, or a mutually agreeable date for the successful candidate.

Purpose of the Position

CFIS’s Director of Finance will be a self-motivated, methodical and conscientious leader. The successful candidate will be a key contributor to the strategic plan and strategic financial plan, will ensure the financial health of the school and the feasibility of strategic decisions, and will support financial activities to allow the school’s Board of Directors to meet its fiscal responsibilities. They will oversee the operations of the school’s Finance and Human Resources Departments, and as such will lead, coach and manage two direct reports for high performance. 
The Director of Finance will be a member of the Senior Leadership Team and will work closely with the Head of School, Assistants Head of School and Departmental Directors.

Job Responsibilities: 

The position’s key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:
Prepare quarterly financial statements and variance analyses for the CFIS Society.
Implement and maintain effective financial policies and procedures to ensure financial integrity.
Provide senior leadership team with monthly departmental/divisional financial reports.
Work closely with senior leadership team and provide financial leadership and strategic insight to the Head of School.  
Lead and coach the Finance and Human Resources Departments to ensure that the department’s stakeholders see the departments as an operational partner in achieving their goals.
Business planning, budget development, and performance measurement.
Preparation of financial information for Alberta Education’s Annual Education Results Report and Three-Year Business Plan, and Annual Operating Plan.
Preparation of annual T3010 Registered Charity Information Return.
In collaboration with the Head of School and senior leadership team, prepare annual budget and financial strategic plan for the CFIS Society.
Maintain internal control system to support the growth and expansion of CFIS.
Lead the Business Office through the year-end external financial audit and any other financial audits by government bodies.
Lead, oversee, and evaluate the business units of the school’s operations and ensure appropriate process mapping, planning, organization, leadership, performance management, and accountability.
Annual issuance of childcare tax receipts.
Monthly issuance of charitable tax receipts and gift-in-kind tax receipts.
Verify and ensure bank covenant calculations on a quarterly basis.
Ensure compliance with Alberta Education’s Level 2 funding requirements and reporting.
Review the Finance and HR Department’s processes, technology and departmental structure to harness the benefits of automation, process modernization and finance effectiveness best practices. 
Continue to ensure the full integration of all business transactions and the accounting system. 
Prepare input for and analyze results of the CAIS benchmarking report.
Attend monthly meetings of the CFIS Society’s Board of Directors and Finance & Audit Committee. 

Qualifications : 

The ideal candidate will bring the following education, experience, skills and competencies:
A university degree from a recognized post-secondary institution and a Chartered Professional Accountant designation (or equivalent).
A minimum of ten years of progressively responsible experience in accounting, audit procedures, and financial operations.
A minimum of three years of experience leading a finance function or a team of at least five.
Demonstrated impact in non-profit or business organizations in a senior leadership position.
Extensive knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), consolidation theory and practice, modern controllership, financial and accounting theories and practices, in order to ensure the appropriate financial framework of the school, provide specialized financial expertise, advice and leadership, and to set accounting standards and ensure compliance.
Ability to present complex financial information to various audiences, and present convincing recommendations for effective and appropriate financial management. 
Solid analytical, organization, planning and problem-solving capabilities.
Able to think both strategically and tactically.
Excellent attention to detail.
Excellent communication skills, preferably in both English and French (English essential).

The successful candidate will need to provide, or have on file, an updated Police Information Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening prior to commencing work. 

Skills, Technical and Behavioural Competencies Required: 

Preference will be given to candidates who:
Are strong planners and organizers.
Have previous experience with non-profit financial management and operations.
Model best practices of exemplary professionalism in dealing with all stakeholders.
Possess strong interpersonal skills that foster collegiality and further the common goals of CFIS’s mission, vision and values.
Have previous experience working in an independent school.
Have experience with finance automation and process modernization. Sage 300 is the school’s current accounting platform.
Experience in the role of Chief Financial Officer in a not-for-profit organization would be beneficial.

Compensation:

We offer a competitive, comprehensive salary and benefits package as well as opportunities for professional growth.
Our benefits include:
Personal days
Sick days
Retirement Savings Benefit
60% tuition discount for children of full-time employees
Extended health and dental coverage
Health and Wellness Spending Accounts
Three weeks paid vacation time off in addition to two-weeks off at winter break and one-week off at March break when the school is closed.

Pay range:
$160,000 to $180,000 annual salary based on education and experience.

Application Process:

This job posting will remain open until filled.
If this position sounds like the perfect fit for you, please submit your cover letter and resume to Apply Now
. Don’t meet every single requirement? At CFIS we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role, but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway with a cover letter and resume describing why you are a great fit and to help us learn more about you. You may be just the right candidate! 

We thank all applicants in advance for their submission.

new_jobs.description:
Corporate Finance Team Overview:

The Corporate Finance team within Canadian Commercial Banking, is part of BMO Financial group and covers both public and large private corporate clients operating in diversified industries. The team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Job Overview

The Associate Director plays a critical role in supporting the growth and risk‑management objectives of the portfolio. This role requires a combination of advanced financial analysis, strong credit analysis and relationship management abilities. Associate Directors contribute to client decisioning, credit structuring, and portfolio oversight, while also supporting new business development and delivering a superior client experience. Work is performed in close partnership with Managing Director and/or Director. The deal team is responsible for marketing, managing, and monitoring large commercial loan portfolios, and also supporting credit requirements and cross selling efforts for other businesses including subordinated debt, equipment leasing, derivatives, cash management, and trade finance. The team assesses financing opportunities of $10,000,000 or more, both on a syndicated and bilateral basis.

Analyzes credit information to support lending decisions and processes for new and existing Commercial banking loans and credit solutions in an assigned portfolio of clients. Makes credit decisions and recommendations in compliance with bank policies and procedures while maintaining an exceptional client service environment.

Negotiates loan structures and terms and conditions that align client requirements with the bank risk appetite and policies.
Assesses client repayment capacity by utilizing financial models and analytical tools to recommend appropriate loan structures and collateral requirements.
Signs off on new, renewal and extension loans within delegated authority.
Monitors portfolio to identify deteriorating credit conditions and compliance, analyses metrics, and assesses broader industry trends to spot risks and opportunities.
Evaluates portfolio performance and recommends capital allocation strategies that optimize returns with investment objectives.
Leads proposal development and delivers presentations to capture new business and expand client relationships.
Networks with industry contacts to gather competitive insights and best practices.
Develops and executes business development plans focused on enhancing client relationships and growth opportunities within the portfolio.
Builds and maintains client relationships to ensure long-term financial performance in collaboration with Relationship Manager and business partners.
Structures and supports new, renewal and extension loans aligned with client needs and bank & risk policies
Conducts financial analysis and risk assessments of clients’ credit information, for an assigned portfolio, to provide insights and make informed decisions
Monitors the portfolio performance for assigned portfolio of Commercial Banking clients on an ongoing basis, taking corrective action when required.
Minimizes BMO’s risk exposure by adhering to credit policies, regulatory standards, and operational guidelines.
Serves as a point of contact for service requests, ensuring expectations are consistently met or exceeded. Escalates issues when needed.
Supports and implements initiatives to enhance service quality, acquire new business and expand client relationships.
Identifies revenue and cross-selling opportunities to enhance portfolio growth.
Identifies share of wallet opportunities.
Leverages analysis tools to nurture and grow a portfolio that exceeds ROE thresholds and evaluates client returns on a proactive basis.
Manages timely and accurate data entry into BMO's systems and leverages the data to support decision-making.
Focus is primarily on business/group within BMO; may have broader, enterprise-wide focus.
Provides specialized consulting, analytical and technical support.
Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

Preferred 5 – 7 years of relevant experience in credit or lending instruments or financial operations in a corporate or banking environment.
If a Credit Qualifiable job, Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the credit portfolio requirements and qualification standards.
Bachelor’s degree required; Business Administration, Finance and Accounting preferred. Any other related discipline or commensurate work experience considered.
Deep knowledge and technical proficiency gained through extensive education and business experience.

Structuring Deals

Advanced level of proficiency:

Problem Solving
Collaboration
Detail-Oriented
Customer Service
Loan Structuring
Regulatory Compliance
Portfolio Management
Credit Risk Assessment
Banking Operations
Microsoft Office

Financial analysis

Salaried
